content.text: NIH ODS distinguishes repeated short, intense efforts such as sprinting or weight lifting from distance endurance activity: creatine may help the former, with little value reported for the latter. Monohydrate is the commonly used supplement form.
No product certification, batch quality, jurisdictional approval or current WADA status has been verified on this page. Ingredient education is separate from those checks.
NIH ODS notes water retention and weight gain. Its healthy-adult safety context does not establish suitability for an individual or for other clinical populations.

content.text: NIH ODS notes possible performance enhancement in athletes, while emphasizing that caffeine content in energy drinks varies. This page does not supply a personal amount or product recommendation.
No product certification, batch quality, jurisdictional approval or current WADA status has been verified on this page. Ingredient education is separate from those checks.
NIH ODS describes nervousness, jitteriness and sleep difficulty; very high amounts can cause serious heart problems. The adult context must not be applied to children or teenagers.
